title: The evidence table serves n without its basis, and drops two whole classes of exclusion without counting them
hypothesis: GET /research/desk/playbook/evidence promises in its own register that exclusions are 'counted, never silently dropped', but it counts only the SIGNAL column's truncations: a horizon leaf that carried no reading at all vanishes uncounted, the baseline column's own truncation count is computed and thrown away, and neither the payload nor the /desk section says how many recorded session dates a cell's n came from -- so serving each cell's already-computed exclusions plus a pooled-signature basis block makes every n readable as what it is.

evidence.measured: 2026-08-12, read-only over the operator's own store (apps/backend/.data/playbook, 10 record files): 4 records sit at the current signature 16a2734d10c91ea7 (2026-06-22, 2026-06-23, 2026-06-24, 2026-08-07) carrying 300 signals. The fold serves 270 cells (9 setups x 2 sides x 15 measures); 132 have n>0 and 84 reach the PLAYBOOK_MIN_N_DISCLOSURE floor of 12 -- and every one of those 84 pools at most those 4 session dates, 3 of them consecutive June days, which the payload never states (other_signatures gets dates + created_span; the pooled signature gets neither). 21 served cells have their n silently reduced by unmeasurable leaves: double_top:short at 1m serves n=31, n_truncated=0 while 59 of its 90 recorded signals carry return_pct: null with the recorded reason 'the 1m horizon is finer than the 5m touch series' (234 of the corpus's 300 signals carry that null 1m leaf); desk_forward._collect_measures:596 does `if measure['return_pct'] is None: continue` with no counter. The baseline column drops its own count at desk_playbook_evidence.py:315 (`baseline_values, _baseline_truncated = baseline_pools[measure]`): capitulation:long at 4h serves n_baseline=8 with no hint that 15 anchors were excluded, beside a signal cell that honestly says n=25, n_truncated=4. Every value needed is already inside the per-file projections PlaybookEvidenceCache stores (session_date, recorded_at, the full forward leaves), so nothing here re-measures anything or changes the cache schema.
evidence.why_promoted: It completes J-08's own acceptance promise ('truncated values excluded from pools with the exclusion disclosed') for the two classes it does not cover, rides one already-registered Data Contract row (no new owner, no new endpoint, no new MCP tool), needs zero new constants and zero parameter changes so playbook_input_signature cannot move, and is sized for one lean iteration.

journey_sketch: Every evidence cell serves the exclusions it already computes (n_unmeasured, the baseline column's own n_truncated/n_unmeasured, n_sessions) and the payload gains a basis block naming the pooled signature's own dates/record count/created span, rendered verbatim on /desk.

title: The whole evidence view rests on 4 recorded sessions, and the act that would grow it is deliberately operator-gated
hypothesis: goal.md's Vision 3 describes a back-scan that walks EVERY recorded session with 5m coverage (~45 sessions at authoring), but the store holds playbook records for only 4 session dates at the current signature -- enlarging that corpus, not any further code, is what would make the distributions worth reading.

evidence.measured: 2026-08-12: apps/backend/.data/playbook holds 10 files across 7 session dates under 3 signatures; only 2026-06-22/23/24 and 2026-08-07 carry the current signature 16a2734d10c91ea7, and their recorded_at timestamps (2026-08-11T13:45:30/45/47Z and 2026-08-11T09:59:58Z) show all four were written by verification lanes, not by an operator back-scan. The three June records were recorded in ~17 seconds total, so corpus size is not a compute constraint. 186 of the 270 served cells sit below the disclosure floor of 12, and open_high_break has fired once ever (2026-06-24), open_low_break once (2026-08-07), cup_handle never.
evidence.why_not_promoted: Not buildable by the dev chain and correctly so: goal.md makes the real back-scan an explicit operator act reported run-or-not-run, and iterations 8-9 built the store-scope guard precisely to stop automated lanes from writing the operator's real store (two anti-goal ledger rows). Proposing a journey that walks the real corpus would re-open the breach that guard closed. Recorded here so the next cycle sees the corpus, not the code, as the binding constraint.

journey_sketch: (operator act, not a dev-chain journey) Run the back-scan over every recorded session with 5m coverage so the evidence pools tens of sessions instead of four, then re-read the distributions with their basis.

title: The back-scan plan cannot tell the operator how much of the store is unwalked without being handed a date range
hypothesis: GET .../backscan/plan classifies only the calendar days inside a From/To range the operator must already know, and deliberately never asks which of them are real sessions, so nothing on /desk answers the one question that decides whether to run it -- how many recorded sessions the store holds and how many carry no record at the current signature.

evidence.measured: 2026-08-12: plan_backscan (desk_playbook_backscan.py:249) walks _planned_dates(from_day, to_day) and returns per-day recorded_at_current_signature / missing_at_current_signature plus total/missing -- with weekends and holidays counted as missing, since the module docstring explains it deliberately never calls desk_sessions.recorded_session_dates (that function reads real bar content, which T-7 bars this GET from paying). The /desk Backscan panel has From/To inputs and no corpus-level count. The store's fine coverage (goal.md build anchors: 5m for all members back to ~2026-06-05) implies tens of walkable sessions against the 4 recorded.
evidence.why_not_promoted: There is no established metadata-only source for 'is this calendar day a recorded session' -- bar_index.db might serve one, but designing that is a real question, not a lean iteration, and getting it wrong either re-introduces the per-GET content walk T-7 forbids or invents a second session-honesty owner beside desk_sessions.py. Lower value and weaker footing than the cell-basis journey.

journey_sketch: The Backscan panel states, metadata-only, how many recorded sessions the store holds and how many carry no playbook record at the current signature, so the operator sizes the act before clicking it.

title: The 4h row of the evidence table is built from the minority of signals that fired early enough in the session
hypothesis: A 4h cell pools only signals whose window fit inside the session, which selects early-session signals systematically rather than randomly, and while n_truncated discloses the count it never says what the survivors have in common.

evidence.measured: 2026-08-12 over the 4 records at signature 16a2734d10c91ea7: at 4h, double_top:short pools 17 values and excludes 73 truncated; double_bottom:long pools 15 and excludes 50; dbi:short pools 4 and excludes 9; range_trade:long pools 28 and excludes 18. At 5m and to_close the same cells pool 83-90 values. The RTH session is ~390 minutes, so a 4h window survives untruncated only for signals triggering in roughly the session's first 150 minutes.
evidence.why_not_promoted: Already disclosed numerically -- every one of those exclusions is served as n_truncated beside the n, which is exactly what J-08's acceptance asked for. The residue is a copy question (a register sentence naming what a 4h pool's survivors have in common), and the era's copy discipline bars anything that reads as an inference about the excluded ones. Too small to spend an iteration on, and it must not grow into a selection-bias claim -- that is era-6 'The Referee' territory.

journey_sketch: The evidence register states plainly what a truncation-excluded pool selects for, without characterising the excluded signals.

title: The whole evidence table can empty out on the next data refresh, and the payload cannot say which of its three hashed inputs moved
hypothesis: GET /research/desk/playbook/evidence lists every non-pooled signature by dates/n_records/created_span and nothing else, so an operator facing an empty or thin cells table cannot tell whether the detector RULES changed (a real regime break that must never be pooled) or merely that the bar-series listing the signature also hashes has grown -- and since every record already carries two of the signature's three hashed inputs verbatim, the fold can name the difference by elimination instead of leaving it to be guessed.

evidence.scan_ref: none (state/pnl-scan.json absent; the post-goal hook logged 'app.research.pnl_scan not built yet -- skipping' at 04:21:30 and 06:33:35, so per proposer-guidance section 4 only surface/dataset work is proposable and no promotion or tuning journey is)
evidence.measured: 2026-08-12, read-only over the operator's own store. apps/backend/.data/playbook holds 10 record files across 7 session dates under THREE signatures; only 16a2734d10c91ea7 is pooled (4 records -- 2026-06-22/23/24 and 2026-08-07 -- carrying 300 signals), while 6 files sit under 898af0960779e897 and 5b70ba860b5efd47 and are served as bare {signature, dates, n_records, created_span}. Each signature maps 1:1 to a distinct playbook_parameters() blob, and diffing those blobs shows the only difference is `setups` (plus base_flatline_max_mbr/handle_desirable_duration_frac, which did not exist in the oldest): every re-key so far was a RULES change, and the payload cannot say so. The next one will not be. compute_playbook_input_signature (desk_playbook.py:322) hashes exactly three things -- the sorted (symbol, timeframe, series_id, checksum) tuples of members union {SPY} at 1m/5m (1,561 series records today across 203 pairs), the config_fingerprint, and the parameters blob -- and BarStore is append-only with every fetch minting a NEW series record (bars.py:930), so a fine-bar top-up moves the signature with no rule change at all. The operator's own top-up ledger shows exactly that cadence: 404 new fine series written on each of 2026-08-05, 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-08 (305 on 08-04), one per (member, fine timeframe), across 23 recorded top-up runs. In that state /desk shows 'No playbook signals recorded at the current signature yet.' (page.tsx:3970) beside 300 recorded signals it will not account for. Every record carries its own `parameters` and `config_fingerprint` verbatim (checked on all 10 files), so two of the three hashed inputs are recoverable from ONE representative file per signature; the third is provable only by elimination, and only when those two match -- which is why the journey forbids claiming `bar_inputs` in any other case.
evidence.also_fixes: the section derives each entry's record count client-side as entry.dates.length (page.tsx:3918) instead of reading the n_records J-11 added to the same payload -- a single-source-of-truth blemish left by the previous cycle, in the exact component this journey touches.

reexamined: The prior cycle's `playbook-real-corpus-is-four-recorded-sessions` was re-examined rather than repeated or reversed. Its core holds and is unchanged: goal.md makes the real back-scan an explicit operator act reported run-or-not-run, and desk_playbook_backscan._SCOPING_ENV_VARS exists precisely so automated lanes cannot write the operator's real store, so no dev-chain journey may walk it. Two things did change. (1) The cost is smaller than assumed -- the three June records were written 15s and 2s apart (recorded_at 13:45:30/45/47), so a full walk of the store's recorded sessions is minutes, not hours; growing the corpus is cheap for the operator. (2) The SEQUENCING now matters: because a fine-bar top-up re-keys the signature, a corpus grown today is unpooled by the operator's own next Refresh Data, and nothing in the product would explain why -- so making the re-key legible ranks ahead of urging the walk, not behind it. Narrowing the signature recipe itself is NOT proposable: it is a goal.md Constraint (the desk_forward recipe, applied at birth) and R-3 rules that even a narrowing clarification needs its own ratification; this disclosure is also exactly the evidence an owner would need to decide that question later.
why_promoted: It rides one already-registered Data Contract row (Evidence aggregates -- same owner desk_playbook_evidence.py, same endpoint, no new row, no new MCP tool), needs zero new constants and zero parameter changes so playbook_input_signature cannot move, reads no bars and costs at most one extra record read per DISTINCT other signature, and is sized for one lean iteration. It is a truth defect rather than a convenience: the state it fixes is not hypothetical but the near-certain consequence of the operator's own near-daily refresh, and in that state today's surface says 'yet' about work that was already done.
journey_sketch: Every listed non-pooled signature also states which hashed input made it other -- parameters (with the changed key names), config_fingerprint, or, only when both recorded pins match, bar_inputs by elimination -- rendered verbatim beside the empty-pool state on /desk.

title: Sizing the unwalked corpus does have a canonical owner -- but a passing journey's own acceptance forbids the plan GET from paying for it
hypothesis: The /desk Backscan panel still cannot say how many recorded sessions the store holds against how few carry a playbook record, so the operator cannot size the act before clicking it.

evidence.measured: 2026-08-12: GET /research/desk/sessions (desk_routes.py:551) IS the shipped single owner of 'which dates in [from,to] are recorded trading sessions', derived from daily bars for at most DESK_SESSION_ANCHOR_LIMIT = 5 anchor members -- a bound desk_sessions.py:68-72 says was chosen deliberately because 'this resolves on a GET'. That corrects the superseded entry, which claimed no established source exists: an owner exists and is already served; only the COST claim was right.

why_not_promoted: J-07's own acceptance -- 'plan GET performs no bar reads (stub-store-that-raises test)' -- is a passing human-authored criterion, so plan_backscan cannot consult that owner, and desk_playbook_backscan.py's docstring (lines 22-35) makes the same choice deliberately. A joint count ('X of Y recorded sessions carry a record at the current signature') computed in the browser would be a new shared value with no owner, which the consistency rule bars. What is left buildable is to render the sessions owner's own count beside the plan verbatim and let the operator join by eye -- a convenience, not a truth defect, since the walk already reports refused_non_session honestly for every weekend and holiday it meets. Ranked below the signature-attribution journey.
journey_sketch: The Backscan panel renders the recorded-session count for its own From/To range verbatim from GET /research/desk/sessions, beside the plan's own recorded/missing counts.
